name: Norway
headline: Norway: +1.1% growth in 2025, 3.0% inflation, debt 54% of GDP
sections: Norway is a $530 billion economy (2025), the world's 32nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.1% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $104K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 6.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 13.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 54% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 44% in 2020. The general government balance is +10.6% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +14.2% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 79% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 26% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.2 years (2024). Population: 5.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
